legal.summary: You can legally sell homemade cookies from your Milledgeville kitchen with a Georgia Cottage Food License. Expect about $190 to get set up and about $175 a year after that. The big limit is that you can sell only directly to customers, not to stores or coffee shops.
key_findings: Cookies are allowed under Georgia's Cottage Food License ($100 a year from the Georgia Dept. of Agriculture), so you don't need a commercial kitchen.
You can sell at markets, events and online within Georgia, but not to stores, restaurants or coffee shops, and you can't ship out of state.
Every bag needs a label with your name and address, ingredients, allergens, weight and the state's cottage food statement.
Starting as a sole proprietor costs nothing extra. An LLC would add $110 to file and $60 a year, and it keeps business debts separate from your savings.
You also need a Milledgeville business license, a free EIN (federal tax ID) and a free Georgia sales tax registration.

legal_setup_cost.source: Georgia Dept. of Agriculture; food handler course; City of Milledgeville (not confirmed)
